label: Mutual funds
note: Facts only. NAV, AUM, returns and expense ratio move — they live in the service, not this repo. What is here is scheme identity: who runs it, what it invests in, which plan and option, and its ISIN.

amc.label: Fund house
amc.note: The asset management company running the scheme. Your money is held by a separate trustee and custodian, so the AMC manages but does not hold it.

scheme_type.label: Scheme type
scheme_type.note: Whether the scheme is open ended, close ended or interval. Open ended schemes can be bought and sold on any business day; close ended ones lock the money until maturity and trade only on an exchange, often below value.

sub_category.label: SEBI sub-category
sub_category.note: The SEBI sub-category, which since 2018 defines what the scheme may hold. It is the only classification that makes two funds genuinely comparable, because it fixes the market-cap or duration mandate rather than leaving it to the scheme's marketing name.

plan.label: Plan
plan.note: Direct or Regular. Direct plans are bought from the AMC without a distributor and carry a lower expense ratio for the identical portfolio; Regular plans embed a distributor commission. The difference compounds over long holding periods.

option.label: Option
option.note: What happens to the scheme's income. Growth reinvests it so it shows up in the unit value; IDCW pays it out, which is taxable in your hands and reduces the unit value by the amount paid.

scheme_code.label: AMFI scheme code
scheme_code.note: AMFI's numeric code for the scheme, which identifies one specific plan and option combination. It is the key that distinguishes the four variants that share a single marketing name.

isin_growth.label: ISIN (growth / payout)
isin_growth.note: The ISIN for the growth option, the globally unique securities identifier. It is the most reliable way to confirm you are looking at exactly the right plan and option.

isin_reinvest.label: ISIN (reinvestment)
isin_reinvest.note: The ISIN for the IDCW reinvestment option of the same scheme.

management_style.label: Management style
management_style.note: Whether the scheme is actively managed or tracks an index. Index schemes follow a rulebook with lower costs; active ones rely on the manager's decisions and charge more for it.

fund_manager.label: Fund manager
fund_manager.note: Who manages the scheme. Not in AMFI's public file and empty on most records here, though it matters for an actively managed scheme because a manager change alters how the mandate is executed in practice.

benchmark.label: Benchmark index
benchmark.note: The index the scheme measures itself against, as declared in its offer document. It is the reference the scheme's own reporting must use, which is why it belongs to the scheme's identity rather than its performance.

launch_date.label: Scheme launch date
launch_date.note: When the scheme opened. Read it with the sub-category, since schemes launched before SEBI's 2018 recategorisation were mapped into their current category rather than built for it.

theme.label: Theme
theme.note: The sector or theme a thematic scheme is restricted to. A narrower mandate means the scheme cannot diversify away from that theme even when the manager wants to.

scheme_full_name.label: Full scheme name
scheme_full_name.note: The scheme's complete registered name including plan and option. Marketing names drop these qualifiers, which is how people end up buying a Regular plan while intending a Direct one.

rta.label: Registrar
rta.note: The registrar and transfer agent that keeps the unit records. It is who you approach for statements and non-financial changes, and it determines which service portal covers this scheme.

riskometer_label.label: Riskometer band
riskometer_label.note: The risk band SEBI requires the scheme to publish, from Low to Very High. It is the AMC's own mandated disclosure, calculated by a prescribed method, and it is reviewed monthly.

min_investment_inr.label: Minimum investment
min_investment_inr.note: The smallest lump-sum purchase the scheme accepts from a new investor.

min_sip_inr.label: Minimum SIP
min_sip_inr.note: The smallest recurring instalment the scheme accepts. It decides whether the scheme is reachable on a small monthly budget.

lock_in_months.label: Lock-in
lock_in_months.note: How long units cannot be redeemed at all. ELSS schemes carry a mandatory three-year lock-in in exchange for the Section 80C deduction; most other open-ended schemes have none.

exit_load_note.label: Exit load terms
exit_load_note.note: The charge for redeeming within a stated period, and how long that period runs. It is a term of the scheme rather than a moving figure, and it is what makes short holding periods costly.

sip_frequencies.label: SIP frequencies
sip_frequencies.note: Which recurring investment intervals the scheme allows.

stp_swp_available.label: STP and SWP available
stp_swp_available.note: Whether money can be moved in or out in instalments through systematic transfer or withdrawal plans, rather than only as lump sums.

demat_available.label: Can be held in demat
demat_available.note: Whether units can sit in a demat account alongside shares, rather than only in the registrar's records.

sid_url.label: Scheme Information Document
sid_url.note: A link to the scheme's SID, the SEBI-mandated document that states the mandate, costs and risks. It is the authoritative source for everything recorded here.

sid_version.label: SID version
sid_version.note: Which version of the Scheme Information Document these facts were read from. AMCs revise SIDs, so this records which document was in front of us.

sanity.note: Riskometer changes monthly and exit load can be revised; both belong in the live layer.
